subject: Pathology
vignette: A 22-year-old woman develops itchy hives over the trunk within minutes of eating shellfish. The lesions are raised, erythematous wheals with pale centers, and each resolves within a few hours. The responsible mediator is released from mast cells and causes arteriolar dilation together with increased venular permeability and itching.
question: Which of the following mediators is most likely responsible for these lesions?

options.text: Interleukin-6
Histamine
C3a
Leukotriene B4
Transforming growth factor beta

explanation_correct: Histamine is the classic mast cell mediator that causes vasodilation and endothelial contraction with increased vascular permeability, and the text also lists it among mediators that sensitize sensory nerve endings to produce pain and itching. In the skin this combination produces the wheal-and-flare urticarial lesion with a raised, edematous, erythematous plaque. The same mediator is named for redness, warmth, swelling, and pain in the cardinal signs of acute inflammation.

explanation_incorrect.A: Interleukin-6 induces hepatic acute-phase reactant synthesis and fever; it is not a vasoactive amine released within minutes.
explanation_incorrect.C: C3a is a complement anaphylatoxin generated by complement activation, which is not the preformed mast cell granule mediator described here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Leukotriene B4 is a neutrophil chemoattractant that also promotes endothelial contraction, but it does not produce the itchy wheal within minutes of food ingestion.
explanation_incorrect.E: Transforming growth factor beta drives fibrosis and angiogenesis during repair and does not cause acute urticarial swelling.

educationalObjective: Histamine from mast cells causes vasodilation, increased permeability, and sensory nerve sensitization, producing urticarial wheals.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 6-year-old boy with a history of atopic asthma and aspirin-sensitive respiratory disease develops acute bronchospasm after taking a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug. His caregiver is warned to avoid this drug class because of the way it shifts arachidonic acid metabolism.
question: Inhibition of cyclooxygenase in this patient most likely produces symptoms by which of the following mechanisms?

options.text: Shunting arachidonic acid toward leukotriene production, increasing bronchoconstriction
Reduced production of prostaglandin E2 in the hypothalamus, lowering the temperature set point
Depletion of mast cell histamine stores in the airway mucosa
Loss of bradykinin-mediated vasodilation in the bronchial circulation
Enhanced neutrophil chemotaxis toward the airways from increased LTB4

explanation_correct: Arachidonic acid metabolites include both cyclooxygenase products such as prostaglandin E2 and lipoxygenase products such as the cysteinyl leukotrienes C4, D4, and E4. The leukotrienes are the mediators named in the text for endothelial contraction and increased vascular permeability, and they are potent constrictors of bronchial smooth muscle. When cyclooxygenase is blocked, arachidonic acid is shunted into the 5-lipoxygenase pathway, so leukotriene formation rises and airway obstruction worsens, which is why NSAIDs can precipitate bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma.

explanation_incorrect.B: Reducing hypothalamic prostaglandin E2 is the intended antipyretic effect of NSAIDs and lowers a temperature set point rather than triggering bronchospasm.
explanation_incorrect.C: Histamine is preformed in mast cell granules and is not depleted by cyclooxygenase inhibition.
explanation_incorrect.D: Bradykinin is generated from kininogen by kallikrein activity and is not a cyclooxygenase product.
explanation_incorrect.E: Neutrophil chemotaxis toward the airway is a leukotriene effect on cells, but the acute bronchospasm here reflects direct leukotriene-induced smooth muscle constriction.

educationalObjective: Blocking cyclooxygenase shunts arachidonic acid into the 5-lipoxygenase pathway, increasing bronchoconstricting leukotrienes in aspirin-sensitive asthma.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 58-year-old man with osteoarthritis takes a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug for chronic knee pain and reports relief of both pain and morning stiffness. The drug reduces prostaglandin synthesis by inhibiting cyclooxygenase.
question: By which of the following mechanisms did this drug most directly relieve his joint pain?

options.text: Reduced prostaglandin E2 synthesis, decreasing sensitization of sensory nerve endings
Inhibition of 5-lipoxygenase, blocking leukotriene generation
Antagonism of cysteinyl leukotriene receptors on smooth muscle
Blockade of histamine release from mast cells
Reduction of bradykinin generation by tissue kallikrein

explanation_correct: Prostaglandin E2 is one of the mediators listed for dolor, acting by sensitizing sensory nerve endings, and bradykinin and histamine share that role. Cyclooxygenase inhibition lowers prostaglandin E2 synthesis, so the threshold for nerve firing rises and pain with stiffness is relieved. The same class of drug also reduces hypothalamic prostaglandin E2 to produce its antipyretic effect, and it diminishes prostaglandin-mediated vasodilation of the redness and warmth of acute inflammation.

explanation_incorrect.B: 5-lipoxygenase inhibitors block leukotriene synthesis; NSAIDs act one step earlier on cyclooxygenase and do not block lipoxygenase.
explanation_incorrect.C: Leukotriene receptor antagonists are used for asthma and do not treat osteoarthritis pain.
explanation_incorrect.D: Mast cell stabilization and antihistamines prevent or block histamine effects, which is not how NSAIDs relieve joint pain.
explanation_incorrect.E: Bradykinin generation depends on kallikrein and kininogen and is not reduced by cyclooxygenase inhibition.

educationalObjective: Prostaglandin E2 sensitizes sensory nerve endings to produce pain, so cyclooxygenase inhibitors relieve inflammatory pain.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 28-year-old woman with severe asthma is started on a medication that blocks the 5-lipoxygenase enzyme, and a second patient is started on a drug that antagonizes the receptor for the cysteinyl leukotrienes. Both drugs reduce airway obstruction provoked by allergen challenge.
question: Which of the following features is shared by the mediators whose production or action these two drugs reduce?

options.text: Synthesis by cyclooxygenase in endothelial cells
Generation from arachidonic acid through the lipoxygenase pathway
Release from preformed mast cell granules on re-exposure to antigen
Induction of hepatic C-reactive protein synthesis
Production of superoxide during the respiratory burst

explanation_correct: The cysteinyl leukotrienes C4, D4, and E4 are products of arachidonic acid generated through the lipoxygenase pathway. They are listed among the mediators of endothelial contraction that increase vascular permeability, and they constrict bronchial smooth muscle. A 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor stops their synthesis and a receptor antagonist blocks their action, so both work on the same mediator family, which is why these agents treat asthma with its bronchospasm and airway edema.

explanation_incorrect.A: These mediators are synthesized by lipoxygenase rather than cyclooxygenase, which is exactly why blocking cyclooxygenase does not remove them in aspirin-sensitive asthma.
explanation_incorrect.C: Only histamine is released from preformed mast cell granules; leukotrienes are synthesized on demand from arachidonic acid.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hepatic C-reactive protein synthesis is induced by interleukin-6, not by arachidonic acid metabolites.
explanation_incorrect.E: Superoxide production is a function of NADPH oxidase during phagocyte killing and is unrelated to leukotriene biology.

educationalObjective: The cysteinyl leukotrienes are lipoxygenase products of arachidonic acid targeted by 5-lipoxygenase inhibitors and leukotriene receptor antagonists.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 34-year-old man with an inflamed insect bite has pronounced swelling that extends several centimeters beyond the puncture site. A tissue biopsy shows widened interendothelial gaps in postcapillary venules with leakage of protein-rich fluid.
question: Which of the following sets of mediators is most directly responsible for opening these interendothelial junctions?

options.text: Leukotrienes C4, D4, and E4, histamine, serotonin, and bradykinin
Interleukin-10 and transforming growth factor beta
C-reactive protein and serum amyloid A
Interferon gamma and interleukin-12
Superoxide and other products of the respiratory burst

explanation_correct: The text names endothelial cell contraction as the mechanism of increased vascular permeability, and specifies that it is mediated by the cysteinyl leukotrienes C4, D4, and E4 along with histamine, serotonin, and bradykinin. Contraction of endothelial cells opens interendothelial junctions so that protein-rich exudate escapes from postcapillary venules and interstitial oncotic pressure rises. Nitric oxide and prostaglandins instead dominate the separate vasodilation that produces redness and warmth.

explanation_incorrect.B: IL-10 and TGF-beta are resolution and healing signals listed as outcomes of inflammation, not as permeability-inducing mediators.
explanation_incorrect.C: C-reactive protein and serum amyloid A are acute-phase reactants produced by the liver; CRP opsonizes rather than causing endothelial contraction.
explanation_incorrect.D: Interferon gamma and IL-12 drive Th1 differentiation and macrophage activation in granuloma formation.
explanation_incorrect.E: Superoxide is a killing product of the respiratory burst and does not produce endothelial contraction of the sort seen here.

educationalObjective: Endothelial contraction and increased permeability are mediated by leukotrienes C4, D4, E4, histamine, serotonin, and bradykinin.
